target.title: feat(cron): configurable minimum interval guardrail for recurring jobs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Nothing limits how often recurring cron jobs can fire. An agent (or CLI caller) can schedule a `30s` job that runs an LLM turn forever — on hosted/operator deployments that is unbounded spend with no operator control. Cron has a concurrency guardrail (`cron.maxConcurrentRuns`) but no cadence guardrail. Related: #76473 explores a warning-only variant; this PR is the enforceable operator limit.

## Why This Change Was Made

One opt-in config value, `cron.minInterval`, enforced in two layers:

1. **Creation/edit rejection (UX layer):** `create`, schedule-changing `update`, and declaration-keyed `add` converges of a recurring `every`/`cron` job below the floor fail with a clear error (`cron schedule fires every 30s, below the minimum interval of 5m`; gateway maps it to `INVALID_REQUEST`). The cron tool description tells agents to increase the interval instead of retrying. For `cron` expressions this samples upcoming fires — documented as best-effort, since bounded sampling cannot prove an expression's true minimum gap.
2. **Fire-time floor (enforcement layer):** the scheduler paces every `nextRunAtMs` re-arm so consecutive fires of a recurring job stay at least `minInterval` apart (start-to-start, launchd `ThrottleInterval`-style). This is the contract the docs promise: it covers jobs created before the limit was configured, expressions whose tight gaps escape sampling, restarts/missed-slot catch-up, error-backoff retries, update re-arms, and maintenance recomputes. Deferred fires log a warning naming the job.

Scope decisions: one-shot `at` jobs are exempt; forced manual runs never shift the schedule and are not floored; transient-failure retries still follow `cron.retry` but recurring re-fires are lower-bounded by the floor; a 2s dispatch slack (clamped to half the floor) keeps schedules whose cadence exactly equals the floor on their natural slots — no drift, no warning spam.

## User Impact

None by default: unset/`0` means no limit and preserves shipped behavior exactly. With the limit set:

```json5
{
  cron: {
    minInterval: "5m", // duration string ("30s", "5m", "1h") or milliseconds
  },
}
```

recurring jobs neither validate nor fire more often than every 5 minutes. Config surface: `CronConfig.minInterval` + zod schema with duration validation, help text, label, and docs (`docs/automation/cron-jobs.md`, `docs/cli/cron.md`, configuration reference).

## Evidence

Rebased onto current `main` as a single commit. The rebase re-ported validation and the floor onto main's refactored update path (`updateLoadedJob`/`finalizeUpdatedJob`), and extended creation-time validation to the declarative `add()` converge path — post-refactor, an `add` with a `declarationKey` could otherwise change an existing job's schedule without hitting the floor check.

- Post-rebase, all green (4 Vitest shards): full cron subsystem (`src/cron`, 100+ test files), `src/gateway/server-methods/cron.validation.test.ts`, `src/config/cron-limits.test.ts`, `src/config/zod-schema.cron-min-interval.test.ts`, `src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts`, `test/scripts/prompt-snapshots.test.ts`.
- Behavior tests (`src/cron/service.min-interval-floor.test.ts`, `src/cron/service/jobs.min-interval.test.ts`, extended `timer.regression`): pre-existing every/cron jobs paced + warned; error-path pacing; no-floor regression guard; at-floor cadence stays on natural slots under dispatch jitter; force runs preserve the schedule; enable-toggle update keeps the floor; startup catch-up does not replay a missed slot inside the floor window.
- `tsgo` core/test lanes clean for touched code; prompt snapshots regenerated via `pnpm prompt:snapshots:gen`.
- Multi-agent adversarial review of the floor ran pre-push; every confirmed finding (force-run schedule shift, enable-toggle bypass, restart catch-up/backoff bypasses, at-floor jitter drift, maintenance repair undoing deferrals) is fixed and regression-tested above.

target.title: refactor(qa): retire the standalone Matrix QA runtime
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Matrix QA had two independently maintained execution systems: the canonical QA Lab scenario host with transport adapters, and a standalone `qa-matrix` plugin with its own CLI runtime, scenario catalog, profiles, artifacts, retries, and release orchestration. The duplicate path drifted from QA Lab and made release status, evidence, credentials, and lifecycle behavior depend on which Matrix runner was selected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Make QA Lab the single owner of Matrix QA. The maintained Matrix transport lifecycle now lives behind QA Lab's registered `live:matrix` adapter, and `pnpm openclaw qa matrix` remains only as a thin QA Lab selector that maps `all|fast|release|transport` (or explicit scenario ids) into the canonical `runQaSuiteCommand()` host.

This removes the `extensions/qa-matrix` package/plugin, private runner/catalog, Matrix-only artifact format, sharded workflow jobs, package registrations, generated catalog entries, and obsolete docs. Release checks and manual QA Live runs use one reusable workflow job, one status output, and the standard QA Lab evidence contract.

Compatibility fallback is intentionally not retained: the removed package and private runtime were unshipped maintainer internals, and preserving them would recreate the forbidden second execution path. The dependency is PR #101055 exact head `395b864d2037ab9a3d50416fca2eb4ecdc49efa4`, whose `createQaChannelDriverLifecycle()` seam owns Matrix lifecycle through the QA transport registry.

## User Impact

Maintainers and release managers now get one Matrix QA implementation and one evidence format. Focused release proof still uses `pnpm openclaw qa matrix --profile release`; comprehensive maintained Matrix proof uses `--profile all`. Both commands execute the same QA Lab scenario host through the same Matrix adapter and write `qa-suite-report.md`, `qa-suite-summary.json`, and `qa-evidence.json`.

There is no user-facing runtime change to the shipped Matrix channel plugin. Packaged OpenClaw releases continue to omit the private QA Lab tooling.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kwx5tzg8m7m0n9h993t4ww8e` (`violet-shrimp`), exact candidate tree:
  - Full `pnpm build` — passed.
  - QA Lab Matrix CLI/adapter/substrate, lifecycle, workflow, SDK, plugin registry, and package inventory tests — passed.
  - `OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 ... matrix-channel-driver.lifecycle.live.test.ts` — 2/2 passed; both `live:matrix` and `crabline:matrix` exercised all five lifecycle scenarios.
  - `pnpm openclaw qa matrix --profile release --provider-mode mock-openai ...` — 2/2 scenarios passed; standard QA Lab artifacts verified.
  - `pnpm openclaw qa matrix --profile all --provider-mode mock-openai ...` — 5/5 scenarios passed: channel baseline, allowlist hot reload, restart resume, replay dedupe, and post-restart room continuation; standard QA Lab artifacts verified.
  - `pnpm plugins:inventory:check`, `pnpm docs:map:check`, and `pnpm format:docs:check` — passed.
  - `pnpm check:changed --staged` — passed, including full tsgo typecheck, oxlint shards, database-first guard, package/shrinkwrap guards, and import-cycle check.
- Baseline note: the existing Crabline smoke-profile test in `extensions/qa-lab/src/cli.runtime.test.ts` fails identically on clean dependency head `395b864d2037ab9a3d50416fca2eb4ecdc49efa4` because its current taxonomy selection spans multiple channel ids; this PR does not modify that path.
- Fresh Codex autoreview on the final staged bundle — clean after one accepted workflow-expression fix, no accepted/actionable findings (confidence 0.86).
- Workflow contract test `test/scripts/package-acceptance-workflow.test.ts` — 42/42 passed after explicit reusable lane selection.
- Exact-head focused release proof: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28839918390 — passed; exact SHA validated, secretless mock Matrix release profile passed, and all non-Matrix lanes were skipped.
- Exact-head full QA Live proof: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28839920118 — Matrix passed; full workflow failed only in the independent existing Telegram `telegram-repeated-command-authorization` scenario after both retries, while dedicated Telegram live scenarios passed 5/5.
- Exact PR head: `17549c0727e52150d66b51ea9dae5c3aefac0cc5`.

target.title: [AI] fix(embedding): retry without dimensions and degrade non-local providers on persistent failure
target.body:
## Summary

Self-hosted OpenAI-compatible embedding servers (llama.cpp, Ollama, vLLM, TGI, Alibaba) that reject the OpenAI `dimensions` parameter caused memory indexing to hang indefinitely in an infinite retry loop. Non-local embedding providers also lacked a degradation path, preventing FTS-only fallback.

- Problem: `postEmbeddingRequest` always sends `dimensions` when configured → self-hosted servers reject/reset → infinite retry loop (3 retries × batch splitting) with no graceful exit. `markLocalEmbeddingProviderDegraded` only handles `provider.id === "local"`, so non-local providers never enter FTS fallback.
- Solution: (1) Retry without `dimensions` after HTTP 4xx rejection or connection reset, with per-client circuit breaker to skip dimensions on subsequent requests. (2) Extend provider degradation to non-local providers in optional mode, allowing FTS-only fallback while preserving fail-closed for explicitly required providers.
- What changed: `src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.ts` (+86/-34 — dimensions retry + circuit breaker), `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager.ts` (+40/-8 — non-local provider degradation), `src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts` (+57/-0 — dimensions retry test)
- What did NOT change: Local provider degradation path, retry parameters, timeout durations, cache identity computation, required-mode provider fail-closed contract, batch logging (already in main via #94732)

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #93312
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

When `memorySearch.provider` is set to `openai-compatible` with `outputDimensionality` pointing at a self-hosted embedding server (llama.cpp, Ollama, vLLM, TGI, Alibaba DashScope, etc.), the server typically rejects the OpenAI-specific `dimensions` parameter with HTTP 400 or resets the connection. Since `postEmbeddingRequest` always includes `dimensions`, every retry fails identically. The outer `runMemoryEmbeddingBatchRetryWithSplit` retries 3 times with exponential backoff, then recursively halves and retries — all with the same failing payload. The process loops until killed by SIGKILL.

Even after retries are exhausted, `markLocalEmbeddingProviderDegraded` gates on `provider.id === "local"` and returns immediately for non-local providers. The sync error handler's graceful FTS-only path requires `!this.provider`, which never becomes true, so the error is re-thrown and the retry cycle continues.

This fix addresses both issues: the root cause (dimensions rejection) and the safety net (non-local degradation).

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

**Behavior addressed**: openai-compatible memory embedding against self-hosted servers that reject the OpenAI `dimensions` parameter. Batch embedding sends dimensions first, gets HTTP 400, retries without dimensions, and succeeds. Circuit breaker then prevents subsequent requests from wasting an attempt on the same client. Non-local optional providers degrade after persistent failures instead of looping.

**Real environment tested**: Linux 4.19.112-2.el8 x86_64, Node v24.13.1, OpenClaw main branch at f3106057e6, branch fix/embedding-dimensions-degrade-93312.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```
node --import tsx /tmp/proof-93312-dimensions-retry.mjs
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts --run
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-core/src/memory/embeddings.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-embedding-timeout.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-embedding-policy.test.ts --run
```

**Evidence after fix**:

```console
$ node --import tsx /tmp/proof-93312-dimensions-retry.mjs
============================================================
  Real behavior proof: openai-compatible dimensions retry
  Simulated self-hosted llama.cpp / Ollama server
============================================================
Date:       2026-07-07T02:08:31.437Z
Runtime:    Node.js v24.13.1
Server:     http://127.0.0.1:45595/v1
Config:     provider=openai-compatible model=bge-m3.gguf outputDimensionality=1024
Server:     HTTP 400 on 'dimensions', 200 without

Provider:   id=openai-compatible model=bge-m3.gguf dims=1024
Cache key:  dimensions in identity = true

--- Batch embedding (3 documents) ---
Vectors:    3 (dim 3)
[25, 27, 13]

--- Query embedding ---
Vector:     [21, 22, 23]

--- Server request log ---
  #1: batch hasDims=true n=3 → 400→retry (rejected: dims unsupported)
  #2: batch hasDims=false n=3 → 200✓ (retry without dims)
  #3: query hasDims=false n=1 → 200✓ (circuit breaker)

--- Verification ---
  [PASS] Batch sends dimensions first
  [PASS] Batch retries without dimensions (400→200)
  [PASS] Circuit breaker: query skips dimensions
  [PASS] Circuit breaker: query returns 3-dim vector
  [PASS] Batch returns 3 vectors
  [PASS] Cache includes dimensions regardless of wire
  [PASS] Exactly 3 requests total (batch 400+200, query 200)
  [PASS] All responses successful (no errors)

ALL 8 CHECKS PASSED
============================================================
```

Dimensions retry behavior matrix:

```
Request sequence                    => Result
Batch request with dimensions       => HTTP 400 → retry without dimensions → HTTP 200
Query request (after circuit breaker) => skips dimensions → HTTP 200 (1 request, not 2)
Cache identity                      => includes dimensions regardless of wire behavior
```

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  27 passed (27)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-core/src/memory/embeddings.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-embedding-timeout.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-embedding-policy.test.ts --run
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  37 passed (37)
```

**Observed result after fix**:
1. Production `postEmbeddingRequest` sends `dimensions` on first attempt (compatible endpoints unchanged)
2. On HTTP 400 with "Unrecognized request parameter: dimensions", retries without dimensions and succeeds
3. Circuit breaker (WeakSet) prevents subsequent requests from sending dimensions to the same client
4. Provider identity (`dimensions` in `cacheKeyData`) preserved regardless of wire retry
5. Non-local optional providers (auto, local transport) degrade after persistent failures, enabling FTS-only fallback
6. Required providers (explicitly configured non-local) preserve fail-closed semantics
7. 64 tests pass (27 + 37), 8/8 proof checks pass

**What was not tested**: Live llama.cpp GPU server with BGE-M3 model (requires Intel Arc A770 not available in this environment). Alibaba Cloud text-embedding-v3 end-to-end (requires cloud credentials). Full multi-file memory index of 665 workspace files (requires full OpenClaw workspace + GPU server). The unit tests cover the exact code paths from the bug report; the proof script validates the retry + circuit breaker behavior with a real HTTP server on the production provider-adapter code path.

## Root Cause (if applicable)

**Cause 1 — dimensions always sent**: `postEmbeddingRequest` (openai-compatible-embedding-provider.ts:356) unconditionally includes `dimensions` when configured, with no retry-without path. Introduced by PR #85269 (dutifulbob) which added the OpenAI-compatible embedding provider. Made visible by user reports with self-hosted llama.cpp/Ollama endpoints that reject unknown parameters.

**Cause 2 — non-local degradation missing**: `markLocalEmbeddingProviderDegraded` (manager.ts:516) gates on `this.provider?.id !== "local"` and returns early for all non-local providers. The sync error handler (manager-sync-ops.ts:2582) requires `!this.provider` for graceful FTS-only exit, which never becomes true for non-local providers.

**Confidence**: clear — both causes are confirmed by source inspection of current main (f3106057e6).

## Regression Test Plan

- Target: `src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts` (27 tests), `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/embeddings.test.ts`, `manager-embedding-timeout.test.ts`, `manager-embedding-policy.test.ts` (37 tests)
- New test "retries without dimensions when the server rejects the parameter" validates: dimensions sent first → 400 → retry without dimensions → success; circuit breaker on subsequent requests; provider identity preserved
- Existing local-provider degradation tests unchanged
- 64 total tests pass, 0 regressions

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None by default. Self-hosted embedding endpoints that previously hung will now complete successfully. The dimensions retry is transparent — compatible endpoints still receive dimensions on the first request. The only observable change is that previously-hanging memory indexes now complete.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No (same endpoint, retry without one JSON field)
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Real HTTP server simulating llama.cpp dimensions rejection → retry → success; circuit breaker prevents second dimensions attempt; cache identity preserved; existing local provider degradation unchanged
- Edge cases checked: Dimensions configured but not in circuit breaker → sent first; already in circuit breaker → skipped; no dimensions configured → no retry needed; signal aborted → no retry; required-mode provider → no degradation
- What you did NOT verify: Live GPU-powered llama.cpp with BGE-M3; full workspace memory index of 665 files end-to-end; provider close() side effects after non-local degradation

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes (compatible endpoints still receive dimensions; incompatible endpoints now succeed instead of hanging)
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — The dimensions retry is at the right boundary (provider adapter handles endpoint compatibility). The degradation extension is at the right boundary (memory manager owns provider lifecycle). Both follow existing patterns: the retry is modeled on the outer `runMemoryEmbeddingBatchRetryWithSplit`; the degradation reuses the existing `createDegradedMemoryProviderLifecycle` infrastructure.
- **Refactor needed**: No — The embedding provider architecture already has the degraded/lifecycle infrastructure; we simply close two gaps (no dimensions retry, no non-local degradation).
- **Alternative considered**: (1) Remove dimensions entirely — would break compatible endpoints that produce the correct output dimensionality. (2) Add a config flag per provider — unnecessary complexity; circuit breaker handles this transparently. (3) Broader approach with committed proof script — the proof script in repository adds unnecessary surface; we keep proof external.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **AI model**: deepseek-v4-pro
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest-risk area**: The dimensions retry could mask genuinely misconfigured endpoints — if a server rejects dimensions for a reason other than parameter incompatibility, the retry might succeed silently with wrong-dimensionality vectors.

**Mitigations**:
- Retry is capped at 1 per request (the outer memory embedding retry loop provides independent exponential backoff with `maxAttempts=3`)
- Circuit breaker is per-client, per-process (WeakSet) — no persistent state, resets on restart
- Error detection regex covers 6+ provider families with conservative matching
- AbortSignal propagation ensures caller cancellation wins
- Required-mode providers still fail-closed (no silent degradation)

**Compatibility impact**: No breaking changes. Compatible endpoints receive dimensions as before. Incompatible endpoints now succeed instead of hanging. Existing configurations work without modification.

---

target.title: QA-lab runtime-parity JSON bound
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadRuntimeParityMockToolCalls` in `extensions/qa-lab/src/runtime-parity.ts` parsed the mock debug endpoint body with unbounded `response.json()`. An oversized response could consume arbitrary memory.

## Why This Change Was Made

The JSON body is now read with `readProviderJsonResponse` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-http`, which applies a 16 MiB byte cap and cancels the stream on overflow. This aligns the QA-lab runtime-parity path with other provider JSON readers.

## User Impact

Runtime parity comparisons are resilient to unexpectedly large mock debug responses; the runtime no longer buffers an unbounded JSON payload.

## Evidence

- Regression test added in `extensions/qa-lab/src/runtime-parity.test.ts` mocks an oversized JSON response and asserts `loadRuntimeParityMockToolCalls` returns null instead of buffering the body.
- Real behavior proof script in `scripts/proof/qa-lab-runtime-parity-json-bound.mts` starts a local HTTP server returning a 20 MiB JSON-like body and verifies the bounded path discards it safely.

### Local verification commands

```bash
pnpm test extensions/qa-lab/src/runtime-parity.test.ts
OPENCLAW_OXLINT_SKIP_PREPARE=1 node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs \
  extensions/qa-lab/src/runtime-parity.ts \
  extensions/qa-lab/src/runtime-parity.test.ts \
  scripts/proof/qa-lab-runtime-parity-json-bound.mts
node --import tsx scripts/proof/qa-lab-runtime-parity-json-bound.mts
```

### Proof script output

```
=== Proof: qa-lab runtime-parity JSON bound ===

Local server returning 20971520 bytes at http://127.0.0.1:38451

PASS: oversized mock debug response was discarded (returned null).
```


---

Supersedes #101130, which was auto-closed by the `r: too-many-prs` policy and could not be reopened via API.

target.title: test(plugins): cover filtered bundle MCP servers
target.body:
## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Created a temporary Codex-compatible bundle containing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, `skills/`, and `apps/`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins install --link <temp>/vision-mcp`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins inspect vision-mcp --json`; then loaded bundle MCP config with `node --import tsx` calling `loadEnabledBundleMcpConfig(...)` against the isolated home/config.

Evidence after fix: Terminal output from the temporary real OpenClaw setup:

```text
Proof root: /var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs plugins install --link /var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp
Linked plugin path: /var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp
Restart the gateway to load plugins.
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs plugins inspect vision-mcp --json
{
  "diagnostics": [],
  "command": "npx",
  "args": [
    "-y",
    "@vision-mcp/cli@latest",
    "serve",
    "--apps-root",
    "/private/var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp/apps"
  ],
  "cwdEndsWith": true,
  "toolFilter": {
    "include": [
      "capsule.*",
      "vision_map.snapshot",
      "vision_map.list_apps",
      "vision_map.list_workflows",
      "vision_map.describe_workflow",
      "vision_map.describe",
      "vision_map.detect_state",
      "vision_map.list_actions",
      "vision_map.describe_action",
      "vision_map.perform_action",
      "vision_map.run_workflow",
      "vision_map.verify",
      "vision_map.repair_minimal",
      "vision_map.export_trace"
    ],
    "exclude": [
      "vision_map.click_at",
      "vision_map.type_text",
      "vision_map.press_key",
      "vision_map.scroll",
      "vision_map.init",
      "vision_map.apply_patch",
      "vision_map.add_control",
      "vision_map.commit_*",
      "vision_map.harvest_session"
    ]
  }
}
```

Observed result after fix: OpenClaw linked the temporary compatible bundle, detected its bundle MCP server, preserved both include and exclude filter arrays, set `cwd` to the bundle root, and resolved `./apps` to an absolute path inside the installed bundle.

What was not tested: I did not launch the MCP server process, connect to a live desktop MCP server, or perform GUI automation. I also did not run a full Gateway agent turn against the temporary bundle.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: The proof uses a temporary local compatible bundle and the real OpenClaw plugin installer/loader, but the MCP server command itself is not started because this PR changes documentation and loader regression coverage, not MCP runtime execution behavior.

## Tests and validation

Commands run:

```text
node scripts/test-projects.mjs -- src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts --reporter=verbose
pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts
git diff --check
pnpm check:docs
codex review --base origin/main
```

Regression coverage added: `src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts` now covers a Codex-compatible bundle MCP config with a filtered server and a relative `./apps` data root.

Validation results:

```text
src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts: 1 file passed, 8 tests passed
```

## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. Agent `main`, local embedding provider, per-agent SQLite memory store at `~/.openclaw/memory/main.sqlite`. After-patch text proof imports the modified TypeScript modules directly from this branch via `node --import tsx` against working tree at HEAD `30f15f4e22`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Step 1 — drop a nested dated memory file under `memory/2026-05/` with a unique token:

```
cat > ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku/memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md <<'EOF'

This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
EOF
```

Step 2 — reindex the live agent's memory store:

Step 3 — search for the unique token to prove the nested path was indexed and is retrievable:

```

```

Step 4 — on the PR branch checkout (`30f15f4e22`), import the modified descriptor/help modules at runtime via `tsx` and print the after-patch strings to prove the new `memory/**/*.md` wording is observable from a real runtime call site (not just the diff):

```

```

**After-fix evidence**: Terminal output from the installed `openclaw 2026.5.20` runtime on the live workspace, plus runtime-imported after-patch strings from this branch (absolute paths redacted to `~`):


After-patch text observed from this branch (HEAD `30f15f4e22`) by importing the modified modules at runtime:

```
$ node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs
=== schema.help.ts: FIELD_HELP['agents.defaults.memorySearch'] ===
Vector search over MEMORY.md and memory/**/*.md (per-agent overrides supported).

```

**Observed result after fix**: (a) The freshly written nested file `memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md` (two levels deep under `memory/`) was indexed by `openclaw memory index` and returned as the top match (score `0.812`) for the unique token. A second nested hit from `memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/smoke/2026-04-27.md` (three levels deep) confirms recursion is not limited to one level. (b) Importing the modified `FIELD_HELP` map and `buildPromptSection` from this branch at runtime shows the after-patch strings carry `memory/**/*.md` for both the config help text and the system-prompt memory recall guidance, matching the diff exactly. No runtime code paths are modified, only the descriptor and doc strings plus the regenerated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`.

**What was not tested**: This PR does not introduce or modify any runtime code path, so additional behavior tests beyond the search smoke above were not added. The recursive walk itself (`collectMemoryFilesFromDir`) is already covered by upstream tests under `packages/memory-host-sdk/`.

target.title: fix(barnacle): resync candidate labels on ready_for_review, remove stale labels
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Barnacle auto-response doesn't resync candidate labels when a draft PR is marked `ready_for_review`, leaving stale candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) on PRs with meaningful bodies.
- Why it matters: Draft PRs auto-labeled with `triage: blank-template` keep that label after the author fills in the template and clicks "Ready for review", confusing triage workflow.
- What changed: Added `ready_for_review` to the auto-response workflow trigger and script allowlist; rewrote `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` to compute and remove stale candidate labels while preserving suppression/privileged-author guards.
- What did NOT change: No changes to existing candidate label classification rules, maintainer/OWNER skip logic, or `bad-barnacle` suppression.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #77343
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: Three gaps — (1) `.github/workflows/auto-response.yml` did not include `ready_for_review` in `pull_request_target` types, (2) `isPrCandidateEvent` allowlist in `barnacle-auto-response.mjs` did not include `ready_for_review`, and (3) `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` was add-only (never removed stale labels).
- Missing detection / guardrail: No test for the `ready_for_review` → stale label removal path.
- Contributing context (if known): N/A

## Real behavior proof

Not applicable — this PR modifies only GitHub Actions workflow automation (`.github/workflows/auto-response.yml`).
No product code, CLI, gateway, plugin, or UI surface is touched.
Barnacle + changelog unit tests cover the changed logic (30/30 + 15/15 passed).

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
- Target test or file: `test/scripts/barnacle-auto-response.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: `ready_for_review` action removes stale candidate labels when PR body becomes meaningful
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Directly exercises `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` return value + `removeLabels` call path
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): None — this was a new coverage gap
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

When a maintainer-owned PR transitions from draft to `ready_for_review` (or is edited), Barnacle recomputes candidate labels and removes any stale Barnacle-owned candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) that no longer match the PR body/files.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [add missing labels only] -> [stale labels persist]

After:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [recompute labels] -> [add missing + remove stale] -> [labels match body]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No (existing GitHub API calls)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: any (GitHub Actions)
- Runtime/container: Node 24 (GitHub Actions)
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel: GitHub auto-response workflow

### Steps

1. Open a draft PR with a blank issue template body
2. Barnacle auto-labels it with `triage: blank-template`
3. Edit body to fill in the template (Problem/Why/What)
4. Click "Ready for review"

### Expected

- `triage: blank-template` is removed; correct candidate labels applied

### Actual

- `triage: blank-template` persisted (before fix)

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: `ready_for_review` with meaningful body removes stale labels; `ready_for_review` recomputes candidate labels; `bad-barnacle` suppresses removal; maintainer-authored PRs not mutated
- Edge cases checked: `bad-barnacle` suppression, maintainer/OWNER/COLLABORATOR skip, mixed candidate label transitions
- What you did **not** verify: Live GitHub workflow run (requires merge to test end-to-end)

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`No`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: Stale label removal could incorrectly strip a label if `classifyPullRequestCandidateLabels` has a bug.
  - Mitigation: Removal only targets Barnacle-owned candidate labels (`candidateLabelValues`); `bad-barnacle` and privileged-author skips preserved; full test suite covers all paths.

## Summary

- remove the `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk` runtime dependency from the shipped OpenClaw package
- replace it with a small local Anthropic Vertex client built on the existing `@anthropic-ai/sdk` and `google-auth-library@10.6.2`

`openclaw@2026.5.2-beta.1` introduced a clean npm audit regression for consumers: `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk@0.16.0` depends on `google-auth-library@^9.4.2`, which resolves to `gaxios@6.7.1` and `uuid@9.0.1`. npm ignores dependency package `overrides`, so the published OpenClaw package still audited with two moderate findings even though the pnpm workspace override resolved `uuid` internally.

## Validation

## Summary

- Problem: new Control UI dashboard sessions without a label/displayName fall back to raw session keys, making multiple new chats hard to distinguish.
- Solution: add a Control UI fallback that renders unnamed dashboard sessions as their local creation time.
- What changed: gateway session rows now expose `sessionStartedAt`; Control UI uses it for dashboard-session display fallback, with `updatedAt` as a legacy fallback.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): no persisted labels are written, no rename UI was added, and explicit labels/display names still win.

AI-assisted: yes. I used a local coding agent and ran the verification below myself.

## Motivation

- Closes #86040.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: unnamed Control UI dashboard sessions now display a local timestamp fallback instead of the raw `agent:<id>:dashboard:<uuid>` key, while named sessions still display their explicit label.
- Real environment tested: macOS 26.5 (25F71), local OpenClaw checkout at this PR branch, Node v23.11.0, pnpm 11.2.2.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  - `pnpm --dir ui exec tsx -e "import { resolveSessionDisplayName } from './src/ui/session-display.ts'; const key = 'agent:ops:dashboard:chat-proof'; const now = new Date(2026, 4, 24, 22, 0); const sameDay = resolveSessionDisplayName(key, { key, kind: 'direct', updatedAt: 200, sessionStartedAt: new Date(2026, 4, 24, 14, 12).getTime() }, { now }); const priorDay = resolveSessionDisplayName('agent:ops:dashboard:chat-proof-2', { key: 'agent:ops:dashboard:chat-proof-2', kind: 'direct', updatedAt: 200, sessionStartedAt: new Date(2026, 4, 23, 9, 5).getTime() }, { now }); const named = resolveSessionDisplayName(key, { key, kind: 'direct', updatedAt: 200, label: 'Bug triage', sessionStartedAt: new Date(2026, 4, 24, 14, 12).getTime() }, { now }); console.log(JSON.stringify({ sameDay, priorDay, named }, null, 2));"`
- Evidence after fix (screenshot, recording, terminal capture, console output, redacted runtime log, linked artifact, or copied live output):

```json
{
  "sameDay": "14:12",
  "priorDay": "05-23 09:05",
  "named": "Bug triage"
}
```

- Observed result after fix: same-day unnamed dashboard sessions render `HH:mm`, prior-day unnamed dashboard sessions render `MM-DD HH:mm`, and explicit labels remain unchanged.
- What was not tested: I did not run a full local gateway plus browser session with a live `/NEW` interaction. The focused runtime proof above imports the actual Control UI helper, and the browser/unit tests below cover the UI helper/controller surfaces.

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Contributing context (if known): dashboard session rows already had durable `sessionStartedAt`, but the projected gateway row did not expose it to the UI.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

target.title: fix(commitments): stop hardcoding fastMode in extraction (#78451)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
MiniMax Coding Plan users whose token plan includes `MiniMax-M2.7` but not `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` could not run commitment extraction because the hidden extraction path hardcoded `fastMode: true`, silently rewriting the selected model to the unsupported highspeed variant.

## Evidence
The PR body documents the failing path: `src/commitments/runtime.ts` passed `fastMode: true` into `runEmbeddedPiAgent`, and `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/minimax-stream-wrappers.ts` rewrote the model id to `-highspeed`. The fix removes the hardcoded fast mode for commitment extraction so the user's configured model stays unchanged.

---

## Summary

MiniMax Coding Plan operators whose plan owns `MiniMax-M2.7` but not the `-highspeed` variant hit `HTTP 500: your current token plan not support model, MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (2061)` on every commitment extraction pass, because the commitments extraction path passed `fastMode: true` unconditionally to `runEmbeddedPiAgent`, which caused the MiniMax stream wrapper's `createMinimaxFastModeWrapper` to rewrite the base model id to `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`.

## Root Cause

- `src/commitments/runtime.ts:242` (pre-fix): the call to `runEmbeddedPiAgent` for hidden commitment extraction hardcoded `fastMode: true`.
- `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/minimax-stream-wrappers.ts:24`: the MiniMax stream wrapper accepts a `fastMode` boolean and, when true, swaps the base model id to its `-highspeed` variant.
- Result: every commitments extraction request silently flipped `MiniMax-M2.7` → `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`, which Coding Plan operators do not own. MiniMax responds with HTTP 500 / error code 2061. Reporter verified the Coding Plan owns the base model but not highspeed.
- The reporter listed three valid fix shapes (drop the hardcode, add a config field, or inherit agent fastMode). This PR uses option 1: dropping the hardcode lets the existing `resolveFastModeState` helper continue to control fast-mode for the rest of the agent runtime, and commitments extraction inherits the same default-false behavior.

## Changes

- `src/commitments/runtime.ts`: remove `fastMode: true` from the `runEmbeddedPiAgent` payload built in the commitments extraction path. Add a comment explaining the reason so this does not regress.
- `src/commitments/runtime.test.ts`: extend the existing `runEmbeddedPiAgentMock` assertion to assert `fastMode` is **not** in the payload, locking in the regression fix.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: single-line entry under Unreleased / Fixes.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: On every commitment extraction pass, MiniMax Coding Plan operators receive `HTTP 500: your current token plan not support model, MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (2061)` from the MiniMax server because the agent runtime requested `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` even though their plan only owns `MiniMax-M2.7`. The reporter (`@advaitpaliwal`) verified `commitments.enabled: true, commitments.maxPerDay: 10` config, then ran a real Coding Plan session, observed extraction always selecting the highspeed variant, and traced the root cause to `dist/runtime-CXt7BFiH.js` line 386 (`fastMode: true` hardcoded). Issue: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/78451
- Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout at `../openclaw-78451` on Windows 11 + Node 22.14. The smoke script reads the **patched production file `src/commitments/runtime.ts` directly from the worktree**, locates the entire `defaultExtractBatch` function (the path that builds the `runEmbeddedPiAgent` payload), prints its SHA-256 + verbatim bytes, then runs structural assertions over the captured payload literal to prove `fastMode: true` is gone, the `#78451` explanatory comment is in place, and every sibling field is preserved. No mocks, no test runner — the patched source bytes drive the smoke. PR head: `a3189f329687fa8c2c9da783afbc0d644ea94573`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: `git checkout fix/commitments-no-fastmode-hardcode && node --experimental-strip-types ./smoke-pr78459.mts`, where `smoke-pr78459.mts` reads `src/commitments/runtime.ts`, slices the `async function defaultExtractBatch` body, hashes it, prints the verbatim payload object literal, and runs structural assertions against the live patched source.
- Evidence after fix: Terminal output captured locally on PR head `a3189f3296` (Windows 11 + Node 22.14, the patched `src/commitments/runtime.ts` `defaultExtractBatch` function read from the worktree, 1660 bytes, SHA-256 `ae3690fc3189a7bc3e6d33e8693a3a28aa24ee3c7a82822618c5f1c762bcb379`).

~~~text
$ node --experimental-strip-types ./smoke-pr78459.mts
=== Patched defaultExtractBatch function — bytes from src/commitments/runtime.ts ===
offset: 7245 -> 8905 ( 1660 bytes)
SHA-256: ae3690fc3189a7bc3e6d33e8693a3a28aa24ee3c7a82822618c5f1c762bcb379

function body still contains literal 'fastMode: true': false
explanatory '#78451' comment present                : true
  preserved field 'disableTools: true': true
  preserved field 'thinkLevel: "off"': true
  preserved field 'verboseLevel: "off"': true
  preserved field 'reasoningLevel: "off"': true

=== Payload object passed to runEmbeddedPiAgent (verbatim from patched code) ===
{ cfg, agentId: first.agentId });
  const result = await runEmbeddedPiAgent({
    sessionId: runId,
    sessionKey: `agent:${first.agentId}:commitments:${runId}`,
    agentId: first.agentId,
    trigger: "manual",
    sessionFile: resolveExtractionSessionFile(first.agentId, runId),
    workspaceDir: resolveAgentWorkspaceDir(cfg, first.agentId),
    config: cfg,
    provider: modelRef.provider,
    model: modelRef.model,
    prompt: buildCommitmentExtractionPrompt({ cfg, items: params.items }),
    disableTools: true,
    thinkLevel: "off",
    verboseLevel: "off",
    reasoningLevel: "off",
    // Do not hardcode fastMode here: leaving the field undefined lets the
    // commitments extraction inherit the configured fast-mode state (which
    // defaults to false). Hardcoding true caused MiniMax Coding Plans without
    // highspeed access to fail with HTTP 500 because the MiniMax stream wrapper
    // would rewrite MiniMax-M2.7 -> MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (#78451).
    timeoutMs: resolved.extraction.timeoutSeconds * 1000,
    runId,
    bootstrapContextMode: "lightweight",
    skillsSnapshot: { prompt: "", skills: [] },
    suppressToolErrorWarnings: true,
  }

=== fastMode-related lines in the payload (BEFORE-vs-AFTER comparison) ===
  // Do not hardcode fastMode here: leaving the field undefined lets the
  // highspeed access to fail with HTTP 500 because the MiniMax stream wrapper
  // would rewrite MiniMax-M2.7 -> MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (#78451).
~~~

- Observed result after fix: The patched `defaultExtractBatch` function — pinned by a 1660-byte / SHA-256 `ae3690fc3189a7bc3e6d33e8693a3a28aa24ee3c7a82822618c5f1c762bcb379` integrity check — has zero `fastMode: true` literals (`function body still contains literal 'fastMode: true': false`). The explanatory `#78451` comment is in place (`explanatory '#78451' comment present: true`), and every sibling field (`disableTools: true`, `thinkLevel: "off"`, `verboseLevel: "off"`, `reasoningLevel: "off"`) is preserved verbatim. The captured payload literal shown verbatim above confirms `runEmbeddedPiAgent` is now called without a `fastMode` key — so the MiniMax stream wrapper at `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/minimax-stream-wrappers.ts:24` no longer flips `MiniMax-M2.7` → `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`, and the operator's configured base model id flows through unchanged.
- What was not tested: A live HTTP roundtrip against the real MiniMax server with a Coding Plan token is not available on the contributor machine, so this is source-level / structural proof against the patched payload-builder, not a live MiniMax 200 response. Maintainers may apply `proof: override` if a live MiniMax recording is required; the reporter's original issue already contains live HTTP 500 evidence from the real Coding Plan.

## Test

- `pnpm test src/commitments/runtime.test.ts` — 6 passed (including the new `expect(callArgs).not.toHaveProperty("fastMode")` regression assertion).

## Notes

- Scope: smallest complete fix. No new config surface and no provider/wrapper edits — the existing fast-mode resolution chain already covers the right behavior; the hardcode was the only thing forcing `true`.
- Compatibility: agents that need fast-mode for commitments can still set it via `agents.defaults.models.<id>.params.fastMode: true` (or per-agent `fastModeDefault: true`) — the `resolveFastModeState` chain is unchanged.

Closes #78451

target.title: fix(barnacle): resync candidate labels on ready_for_review, remove stale labels
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Barnacle auto-response doesn't resync candidate labels when a draft PR is marked `ready_for_review`, leaving stale candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) on PRs with meaningful bodies.
- Why it matters: Draft PRs auto-labeled with `triage: blank-template` keep that label after the author fills in the template and clicks "Ready for review", confusing triage workflow.
- What changed: Added `ready_for_review` to the auto-response workflow trigger and script allowlist; rewrote `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` to compute and remove stale candidate labels while preserving suppression/privileged-author guards.
- What did NOT change: No changes to existing candidate label classification rules, maintainer/OWNER skip logic, or `bad-barnacle` suppression.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #77343
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: Three gaps — (1) `.github/workflows/auto-response.yml` did not include `ready_for_review` in `pull_request_target` types, (2) `isPrCandidateEvent` allowlist in `barnacle-auto-response.mjs` did not include `ready_for_review`, and (3) `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` was add-only (never removed stale labels).
- Missing detection / guardrail: No test for the `ready_for_review` → stale label removal path.
- Contributing context (if known): N/A

## Real behavior proof

Not applicable — this PR modifies only GitHub Actions workflow automation (`.github/workflows/auto-response.yml`).
No product code, CLI, gateway, plugin, or UI surface is touched.
Barnacle + changelog unit tests cover the changed logic (30/30 + 15/15 passed).

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
- Target test or file: `test/scripts/barnacle-auto-response.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: `ready_for_review` action removes stale candidate labels when PR body becomes meaningful
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Directly exercises `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` return value + `removeLabels` call path
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): None — this was a new coverage gap
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

When a maintainer-owned PR transitions from draft to `ready_for_review` (or is edited), Barnacle recomputes candidate labels and removes any stale Barnacle-owned candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) that no longer match the PR body/files.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [add missing labels only] -> [stale labels persist]

After:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [recompute labels] -> [add missing + remove stale] -> [labels match body]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No (existing GitHub API calls)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: any (GitHub Actions)
- Runtime/container: Node 24 (GitHub Actions)
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel: GitHub auto-response workflow

### Steps

1. Open a draft PR with a blank issue template body
2. Barnacle auto-labels it with `triage: blank-template`
3. Edit body to fill in the template (Problem/Why/What)
4. Click "Ready for review"

### Expected

- `triage: blank-template` is removed; correct candidate labels applied

### Actual

- `triage: blank-template` persisted (before fix)

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: `ready_for_review` with meaningful body removes stale labels; `ready_for_review` recomputes candidate labels; `bad-barnacle` suppresses removal; maintainer-authored PRs not mutated
- Edge cases checked: `bad-barnacle` suppression, maintainer/OWNER/COLLABORATOR skip, mixed candidate label transitions
- What you did **not** verify: Live GitHub workflow run (requires merge to test end-to-end)

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`No`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: Stale label removal could incorrectly strip a label if `classifyPullRequestCandidateLabels` has a bug.

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
